articles.title: Lipoic acid-conjugated chalcones exert antitumor activity via ROS elevation and ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Overcoming drug resistance and minimizing off-target toxicity remain major challenges in cancer therapy. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target. Natural chalcones exhibit antitumor properties linked to oxidative stress induction, yet efficacy and selectivity are limited. To achieve this, we designed and synthesized a series of novel α-lipoic acid (LA)-conjugated chalcone derivatives with the aim of disrupting redox and iron homeostasis to induce ferroptosis in cancer cells. Here, we report that these conjugates elevate reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels most prominently in T24 bladder cancer cells, compared to other tested cell lines, leading to potent growth inhibition and suppressed migration. Mechanistically, RNA-seq and functional assays reveal that the lead compound CA-LA triggers ferroptosis by dysregulating cellular iron and glutathione metabolism. Our work presents a rational design strategy for redox-directed antitumor agents and identifies LA-chalcone hybrids as promising candidates for selective bladder cancer therapy via ferroptosis induction.

articles.title: Glut1 and MCT4 cooperatively promote ccRCC cell proliferation and are associated with glycolytic reprogramming and immune-related alterations.
articles.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by glycolytic reprogramming and a lactate-rich tumor microenvironment. We integrated multi-omics, single-cell, tissue microarray, and in vitro analyses to investigate the roles of Glut1 and MCT4 in ccRCC. Both transporters were upregulated at the mRNA and protein levels, enriched in tumor epithelial cells, and located within a glycolysis-associated co-expression module. Elevated MCT4 expression and combined Glut1/MCT4 dysregulation were associated with poor overall survival, while a glycolysis-related random forest model improved prognostic prediction. Functionally, Glut1 and MCT4 exhibited reciprocal expression changes and promoted cell proliferation and cell-cycle progression. Combined knockdown produced a greater inhibitory effect than either individual knockdown in both 786-O and Caki-1 cells. Computational analyses further associated Glut1/MCT4 expression with immune-related features and predicted immunotherapy response, whereas metabolomics revealed elevated lactate and ribose 5-phosphate levels. Collectively, these findings identify a coordinated Glut1-MCT4 axis associated with proliferative, metabolic, prognostic, and immune-related features in ccRCC, although further mechanistic and in vivo validation is required.

articles.title: Head-to-head comparison of quantitative perfusion parameters derived from DECT, IVIM, and DCE-MRI for renal mass characterization: a within-patient, prospective study.
articles.abstract: Accurate characterization of solid renal masses is essential because management and outcomes differ substantially by histologic subtype. Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the most common and aggressive RCC subtype, is also the most responsive to targeted anti-angiogenic therapies. Quantitative perfusion imaging may enable a noninvasive "virtual biopsy" approach, but the comparative performance of dual-energy CT (DECT), intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM), and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) remains unclear. This study compared perfusion biomarkers from these modalities for differentiating ccRCC from other solid renal masses. In this prospective single-center study, adults with solid renal masses underwent preoperative DECT, IVIM, and DCE-MRI, with postoperative histopathology as the reference standard. DECT-derived iodine concentration (IC) and iodine ratio (IR), IVIM-derived perfusion fraction (f) and pseudodiffusivity (D*), and DCE-MRI-derived wash-in rate (WIR), wash-out rate (WOR), and area under the time-intensity curve (AUTIC) were evaluated. Diagnostic performance for differentiating ccRCC from other solid renal masses was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Thirty-three patients (mean age, 49.8 ± 11.9 years; 21 men) were included. Compared with other solid renal masses, ccRCC demonstrated significantly higher IC and IR (p < 0.02) and higher AUTIC and WIR (p < 0.05). IVIM parameters did not differ significantly (p > 0.05). IC achieved the highest diagnostic performance across readers (AUC, 0.79-0.83). After exclusion of benign tumors, IC demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUC, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.89-1.00). Multivariable models did not improve performance over the best individual parameter. DECT and DCE-MRI perfusion biomarkers showed comparable performance for differentiating ccRCC from other solid renal masses, whereas IVIM provided limited diagnostic value. The lack of incremental benefit from multiparametric modeling suggests that DECT-derived iodine concentration alone may be sufficient for clinical virtual biopsy workflows, particularly when MRI is unavailable or contraindicated.

articles.title: FGFR-altered urothelial carcinoma in the EV-pembrolizumab era: Rationale and emerging data for upfront triplet strategies.
articles.abstract: Urothelial cancer (UC) is a common malignancy with a significant incidence worldwide, particularly in Europe and North America. Approximately 5% of patients have de novo metastatic disease at the time of initial diagnosis. The combination of Enfortumab vedotin and Pembrolizumab recently transformed the first-line treatment landscape, providing better clinical outcomes and greater tolerability compared to traditional cisplatin-based therapies. However, alterations in fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling may diminish the effectiveness of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs), underscoring the need for novel combination therapies. This review examines emerging evidence supporting combination strategies incorporating pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in FGFR-altered urothelial carcinoma, focusing on their potential integration with first-line doublet regimens. Ongoing and future clinical studies will be essential to define the clinical value of these combinations and to advance precision immunotherapy strategies guided by genomic alterations, to improve outcomes for patients with UC.

articles.title: Sympathetic innervation of renal cell carcinomas and their environment, a pilot study.
articles.abstract: Sympathetic nerves are a common feature in tumors; in the tumor microenvironment and in mouse models, they have been implicated in tumor initiation and progression. Clinical studies report an association between increased nerve density and adverse tumor characteristics in various carcinomas. So far, no studies have been published in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). The aim of this study is to quantify sympathetic nerves in RCC and its environment. We quantified sympathetic nerve density in 10 T1a RCCs, 5 metastatic lesions, and 8 normal kidney tissues. Histopathological analysis and immunohistochemistry with antibodies against tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) were performed. In normal kidney, autonomic nerves were mainly sympathetic. Within the T1a tumors, the percentage of TH-positive pixels of sympathetic nerves was low (0.03 +/- 0.05), and very low in metastases (0.001 +/- 0.003). A remarkable high-density pattern of sympathetic fibers was found in the vicinity of two T1a tumors. More distant (> 2mm), the percentage of TH-positive pixels was similar to that of controls (0.11 +/- 0.10). We observed a low density of sympathetic nerves within T1a renal tumors and metastatic lesions compared with normal kidney tissue. An increased density of sympathetic nerves was seen in the direct vicinity of two tumors. These preliminary results in this small pilot cohort suggest that in RCC, increased sympathetic nerve density may be encountered in the tumor environment but not the tumor itself.

articles.title: Splenic toxicity and gene expression alterations induced by perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS) ingestion in Sprague Dawley rats.
articles.abstract: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are synthetic chemicals widely used in industrial and consumer products. Chronic exposure to PFAS has been associated with adverse health outcomes, including kidney cancer, thyroid dysfunction, pregnancy complications, and liver damage. This study investigates the splenic toxicity of perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS), a short-chain PFAS compound composed of a four-carbon backbone bonded to fluorine atoms and a sulfonic acid functional group. PFBS is commonly found in wastewater, household dust, and cleaning agents. To assess its biological impact, Sprague Dawley rats were fed diets containing varying concentrations of PFBS. Histological analysis of the spleen revealed no overt structural damage and molecular profiling indicated significant alterations in gene expression. SYK, a spleen tyrosine kinase protein increased in PFBS exposed groups. A significant increase in the rat weight of exposed groups and marginally inflamed spleens may suggest some effects of PFBS ingestion on the treated animals. Transcripts associated with T-cell regulation and protein phosphorylation were upregulated, while inflammatory and immune-related genes were downregulated. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels showed slight elevation in PFBS-exposed groups, and animals receiving higher doses exhibited increased body weight compared to controls. These findings suggest that dietary ingestion of PFBS induces subtle but measurable toxicological effects on splenic function and immune regulation, probably indicating further research into its long-term health implications.

articles.title: Prognostic impact of lenvatinib dose intensity in previously untreated patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma receiving lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab.
articles.abstract: Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab is the standard of care as first-line systemic therapy for advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC). However, the prognostic impact of the relative dose intensity (RDI) of lenvatinib remains unclear. Clinical data from 54 patients with advanced RCC who received lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab as first-line therapy were retrospectively evaluated. The RDI of lenvatinib within the initial 3 months (3m-RDI) was calculated, and tumor response and survival were compared according to 3m-RDI. The 3m-RDI threshold was set at 70%, which was significantly associated with objective response during treatment. Patients with a high 3m-RDI (≥70%) had a higher objective response rate (ORR) than those with a low 3m-RDI (<70%) (69% vs. 36%, P = .014).Multivariable analysis identified 3m-RDI ≥70% as an independent predictor of higher ORR (odds ratio: 5.25, 95% CI: 1.55-20.36, P = .007). Among patients with synchronous metastasis (n = 24), patients with a high 3m-RDI had higher ORR (62% vs. 18%, P = .028) and longer progression-free survival (median: not reached vs. 4.8 months, P = .035) than those with a low 3m-RDI. Lenvatinib with 3m-RDI ≥70% may be a useful early treatment-related marker associated with clinical outcomes during first-line lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab for advanced RCC.

articles.title: ARHGAP40 suppresses clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression and is associated with altered glutamine-related metabolism and redox balance.
articles.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by marked molecular and metabolic heterogeneity. This study investigated the functional role of ARHGAP40 in ccRCC and examined signaling and metabolic changes associated with ARHGAP40 expression. TCGA-KIRC and DiseaseMeth datasets were used to analyze ARHGAP40 expression and promoter methylation. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments evaluated malignant phenotypes in vitro, and an ARHGAP40-overexpression xenograft model was used to assess tumor growth. Co-immunoprecipitation and RhoA activity assays assessed ARHGAP40-RhoA interaction and RhoA activation, while PI3K/AKT signaling, glutamine metabolism, GSH/GSSG, and ROS levels were examined. Rescue experiments were performed using SC79, RhoA-Q63L, and NAC. ARHGAP40 was downregulated in ccRCC and was associated with increased promoter methylation. ARHGAP40 overexpression suppressed cell proliferation, migration, invasion, EMT, and xenograft growth, while promoting apoptosis and G1-phase arrest; ARHGAP40 knockdown produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, ARHGAP40 was associated with RhoA, and its overexpression was accompanied by reduced RhoA activity and PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. ARHGAP40 overexpression also reduced intracellular glutamine and glutamate levels and net glutamine consumption, decreased the GSH/GSSG ratio, and increased ROS levels. SC79 and RhoA-Q63L partially reversed the biological and redox effects induced by ARHGAP40 overexpression, whereas NAC reversed the redox changes. ARHGAP40 acts as a tumor suppressor in ccRCC. Our findings support a functional link between ARHGAP40, RhoA-PI3K/AKT signaling, glutamine-related metabolism, and cellular redox balance.

articles.title: PRMT7 at the crossroads of cancer progression and therapeutic targeting (Review).
articles.abstract: Protein arginine methyltransferase 7 (PRMT7), the sole type III PRMT family member, catalyzes arginine monomethylation and has recently emerged as an important regulator of cancer biology. Increasing evidence indicates that PRMT7 participates in tumor initiation and progression through epigenetic regulation, transcriptional control, RNA processing and signaling pathway modulation. Dysregulated PRMT7 expression has been reported in diverse malignancies, including leukemia, breast cancer, lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer and gastric cancer. Functionally, PRMT7 has been implicated in epithelial‑mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, metastasis and immune modulation, although its effects may vary depending on cellular and tumor context. The present review summarizes the structural and biochemical features of PRMT7, its mechanistic roles across different cancer types, and its potential as a therapeutic target. Recent progress in PRMT inhibitor development was also discussed, with particular emphasis on PRMT7‑selective compounds such as SGC3027, SGC8158 and JS1310, as well as the key challenges that remain for clinical translation. Elucidating the context‑specific functions and targetable vulnerabilities of PRMT7 may provide new opportunities for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: TFEB-Amplified Renal Cell Carcinoma With Focal Rhabdoid Features, Hyaline Globules, Giant Tumor Cells, and Osseous Metaplasia.
articles.abstract: TFEB-amplified renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a rare, molecularly defined RCC, characterized by amplification of the TFEB gene on chromosome 6p21.1, with fewer than 100 tumors reported to date. Herein, we report a TFEB-amplified RCC with focal rhabdoid features, hyaline globules, giant tumor cells, and osseous metaplasia. This tumor further expands the histological spectrum of TFEB-amplified RCC. A 59-year-old man underwent radical nephrectomy for a 7.6-cm left renal mass. Histologically, the tumor demonstrated predominantly papillary architecture (90%) with focal solid areas (10%). Tumor cells showed voluminous eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Additional findings included multifocal rhabdoid features (10%), intracellular hyaline globules, giant tumor cells, occasionally with multinucleation, osseous metaplasia, psammomatous calcifications, and focal tumor necrosis (5%). The tumor was classified as World Health Organization (WHO)/International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grade 4 and staged as pT2aNx. Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells were positive for PAX8, AMACR, and HNF1β, with rare Melan-A expression, and negative for keratin 7, CA9, GATA3, p63, ALK, cathepsin K, HMB45, and TFE3. RCC not otherwise specified (NOS) was initially diagnosed, and molecular testing was subsequently performed to further assist in the diagnosis. Chromosomal microarray analysis demonstrated amplification of chromosome 6p21.1 involving TFEB and other genes with a reported copy number of ≥7, which was confirmed by fluorescence in situ hybridization demonstrating TFEB copy-number gain with up to 9 TFEB signals per nucleus. Based on the morphology, immunoprofile, and molecular findings, the tumor was classified as TFEB-amplified RCC. The patient subsequently developed widespread metastatic disease and received radiotherapy and systemic treatment. He remains alive with progression of disease at 45 months of follow-up.

articles.title: Late-onset Mycobacterium bovis prosthetic knee infection following intravesical BCG therapy.
articles.abstract: Intravesical BCG is a common treatment for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer but can rarely cause serious infections. We report the case of a man in his late 60s with bilateral total knee replacements who developed knee pain 18 months after receiving BCG therapy. Evaluation revealed mildly elevated inflammatory markers, negative routine bacterial cultures and acid-fast culture positive for Mycobacterium bovis, resistant to pyrazinamide. Imaging demonstrated periprosthetic lucency without overt mechanical failure. Following multidisciplinary discussion, the patient was treated with isoniazid, rifabutin and pyridoxine without surgical intervention. His symptoms resolved and he remained free of infection at 3 years of follow-up. Few cases of BCG-related prosthetic knee infections have been described. This case underscores that prosthetic joint infection can occur long after BCG therapy and that carefully selected patients may be managed successfully with prolonged antimycobacterial therapy.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "RUNX2 enhances bladder cancer progression by promoting glutamine metabolism" [Neoplasia 60 (2025) 101120, doi: 10.1016/j.neo.2024.101120].
CYP24A1 rs1570669 and rs2762934 polymorphisms and bladder cancer susceptibility: a Turkish case-control study.
articles.abstract: Bladder cancer (BC) is one of the most common malignant tumours of the urinary system and represents an important public health problem. Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are common human genetic variations and may affect cancer risk by altering various genetic processes such as vitamin D metabolism and tumour suppression. CYP24A1 rs1570669 and rs2762934 polymorphisms may be relevant to cancer biology through their potential effects on the degradation of active vitamin D metabolites. These polymorphisms have been associated with the risk of urinary cancer, including BC, in an Asian population. To the best of our knowledge, the impact of CYP24A1 rs2762934 and rs1570669 variants on BC susceptibility has not yet been investigated in any Caucasian cohort. Consequently, this study represents the first attempt to evaluate their associations with BC risk within a Turkish population. The present study investigated CYP24A1 gene polymorphisms in 152 BC patients and 178 healthy controls using a TaqMan allelic discrimination assay with real-time PCR (qPCR). Neither polymorphism was significantly associated with BC risk, although the A alleles of both variants showed a non-significant trend towards increased odds of BC. Additionally, both groups differed significantly regarding age, BMI, and smoking status, but not regarding other characteristics, such as vitamin D levels. The CYP24A1 rs2762934 and rs1570669 polymorphisms were not significantly associated with BC susceptibility in this Turkish cohort. Despite this, the A alleles of both variants showed a non-significant trend toward increased odds of BC, which may warrant further investigation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Biological evaluation and in vivo degradation steady-state endpoint exploration of a sodium alginate/poloxamer composite temperature-sensitive embolic gel for tumors.
articles.abstract: In the regulatory science of absorbable medical devices, traditional in vivo degradation evaluations are often hindered by lengthy evaluation cycles and ambiguous standards. This restricts the research, development, and translation of novel embolic materials. The lack of an evaluation system to determine whether tissue responses have reached a "degradation steady-state endpoint" is particularly critical. This study systematically evaluated the biological efficacy and in vivo degradation steady state of a composite temperature-sensitive embolic agent based on sodium alginate and poloxamer. This gel undergoes a spontaneous phase transition at body temperature. Combined with a dual-lumen microcatheter delivery technique, it achieves instant crosslinking with calcium ions, exhibiting excellent resistance to blood flow washout. The embolization results in canine hepatic and renal artery models and rabbit renal tumor in situ models confirmed the efficacy of this composite gel as a tumor embolic agent. Its ability to induce coagulation necrosis and apoptosis in tumor tissues outperformed current clinical lipiodol and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) microspheres. A six-month porcine hepatic/renal artery study examined residual implant-like material, recanalization, local histopathology, selected endothelial markers, and systemic observations. Under the tested protocols, the PS gel occluded target vessels and showed good biological safety. In pigs, implant-like material remained at six months, while selected histological injury and inflammatory measures were lower than at earlier terminal time points. Histopathological results indicated that local macrophage phagocytosis and inflammatory responses in the target vessels were active between 1 and 3 months. By 6 months, the inflammation level had significantly subsided to a mild state, with concurrent reductions in fibrosis and fatty infiltration. This was accompanied by prominent tissue repair and remodeling, marking a smooth transition of the tissue response toward a steady state. The results support a candidate criteria-based framework for future prospective evaluation. The results justify further formulation characterization, controlled long-term studies, and component-resolved degradation analysis.

Proteasuria: extending an existing term into a framework for concentration-based and catalytic protease diagnostics in urine, with emphasis on activity-based methods.
articles.abstract: Proteases are central to cancer pathobiology and attractive targets for noninvasive diagnosis. Diagnostic use of urinary proteases has developed along two methodologically distinct streams: measurement of protein abundance by immunoassay and increasingly by mass spectrometry, and direct measurement of enzymatic activity using peptide substrates. However, no common terminology unifies these approaches. This narrative review synthesizes evidence published between 2016 and 2026, concentrating on urine and, for the transferability of the methodology, on fecal water and serum. Saliva and seminal fluid are surveyed only to show that protease biomarkers there are measured by abundance alone. It adopts, from its existing use in nephrology, the term proteasuria as a unifying construct for the urinary protease diagnostic field, proposing a wider scope than the pathophysiological sense in which it was introduced. Two operational subtypes are defined: concentration-based and catalytic proteasuria. The distinction rests on the parameter measured rather than on the detection chemistry. Within the catalytic subtype single-enzyme detection using a selective substrate is distinguished from disease profiling using a multi-substrate panel. Evidence was identified by a PubMed search supplemented by citation and semantic search and screened by a single reviewer without protocol registration or formal risk-of-bias assessment. Concentration-based proteasuria is the clinically established stream, yet no urinary analyte has displaced cystoscopy, and approved assays remain insufficient as stand-alone rule-out or triage tests. The catalytic stream rests mainly on small single-center case-control studies reporting activity qualitatively; only one reports formal diagnostic performance, with a single elastase-specific substrate in 12 cases and 24 controls, and no head-to-head comparison with concentration-based assays has been published. Analytical validity is partial: substrate selectivity is established by combinatorial screening and confirmed with inhibitor and orthogonal controls, but precision, limits of quantification in urine and inter-laboratory reproducibility are not systematically reported, and no reference material or external quality-assessment scheme exists for this assay class. A largely independent exogenous stream of synthetic urinary biomarkers and activity-based nanosensors reports high accuracy, but all published diagnostic-accuracy data derive from animal models. On a translational-readiness scale the urinary catalytic stream is proof-of-concept, research-grade work, and any realistic target is therefore not cystoscopy but the margin at which established assays fail, principally low-grade noninvasive disease. The same reasoning identifies the detection of advanced adenoma, for which the fecal immunochemical test performs poorly, as the concrete benchmark for extending the framework to fecal protease profiling in colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Chromogenic and FRET peptide substrates, quantum-dot peptide conjugates and electrochemical peptide interfaces: A 25-year journey from combinatorial chemistry to clinical readouts-A viewpoint.
articles.abstract: This Viewpoint synthesises 25 years of work from a single laboratory on activity-based protease sensing and offers a critical appraisal of where each of the three resulting platforms stands today. The activity of proteolytic enzymes-rather than their abundance-determines the outcome of inflammation, tumour progression, viral entry and barrier dysfunction. Measuring it in clinical samples is demanding: closely related proteases share substrate preferences, and biological matrices are crowded with endogenous inhibitors and competing hydrolases. Over the past 25 years, our group at the University of Gdansk has developed a chemical toolkit along three complementary axes, assembled here, as a probe ladder running from solution chemistry to solid-state interface. First, internally quenched chromogenic and Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) peptide substrates, designed by iterative deconvolution of combinatorial libraries spanning non-primed and primed subsites, provide selective readouts for serine, cysteine, metallo- and viral proteases. Second, peptide-quantum dot conjugates built on non-toxic ZnO nanocrystals improved detection limits 20-30-fold over the parent solution substrate in two published demonstrators. Third, peptide-modified gold electrodes translate protease cleavage and molecular recognition into a label-free electrochemical signal-exemplified by an electrode that reads 20S proteasome activity and by an antimicrobial-peptide interface for bacterial endotoxin. We applied the resulting probes in exploratory studies of bladder cancer, type-2 diabetes and diabetic nephropathy, and positioned them within the broader landscape of activity-based protease sensing-the activity-based probes of the Bogyo and Cravatt laboratories, the PS-SCL and HyCoSuL combinatorial approaches, and the Weissleder near-infrared imaging program.

articles.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma With Sarcomatoid Dedifferentiation: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Metastatic sarcomatoid renal cell carcinoma (msRCC) is an aggressive disease typically associated with poor outcomes following VEGF-targeted therapies. This study evaluated in real-world outcomes in patients with msRCC based on whether they received treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). We conducted a multi-institutional, retrospective study of patients who received systemic therapy for msRCC between July 2010 and June 2020. In total, 203 patients across 6 US academic centers were included. Patients were categorized into 2 groups based on whether they received ICIs: ICI+ (n=155) and ICI- (n=48). Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and measured from the initiation of frontline systemic therapy. Treatment responses were evaluated by investigators at participating centers. After a median follow-up of 48.1 months, OS was significantly longer in the ICI+ group (median OS, 31.0 vs 7.6 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.38; 95% CI, 0.26-0.56; P<.001). ICI+ status (HR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.25-0.59; P<.001), non-clear cell or unclassified histology (HR, 2.99; 95% CI, 1.86-4.79; P<.001), and sarcomatoid component ≥25% (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.11-2.59; P=.015) were independently predictive of OS. OS benefit in ICI+ group was maintained in the second line or later (median OS, 39.6 vs 7.6 months; HR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.21-0.49; P<.001). Among patients with non-clear cell or unclassified histology, the ICI+ group had longer OS (median, 18.1 vs 7.0 months; HR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.09-0.44; P<.001). Objective (39.4% vs 18.8%; P=.014) and complete (11.0% vs 4.2%; P=.258) response rates were higher in the ICI+ group. A potential benefit of ICI-based therapy is suggested in both clear cell and non-clear cell msRCC. The benefit was observed in both the first-line setting and in second-line or later lines of therapy.

articles.title: AXL and enolase 2 associate with therapy resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors lenvatinib and cabozantinib in renal cancer cells.
articles.abstract: Resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) remains a major clinical challenge in the treatment of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). In this study, we established renal cancer cell models resistant to the TKI lenvatinib and cabozantinib to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired resistance. Using a quantitative proteomic approach, we profiled protein alterations associated with the resistant phenotype. A moderate-to-strong linear correlation was observed between the proteomic profiles of drug-treated control cells and matched resistant cells (Pearson r = 0.80 for lenvatinib and r = 0.66 for cabozantinib), suggesting shared alterations associated with the resistant phenotype. Notably, 35 proteins were commonly upregulated, and 40 proteins were commonly downregulated, across both resistant models, highlighting shared adaptive mechanisms driving cross-resistance. Among these, AXL tyrosine kinase receptor and enolase 2 (ENO2) emerged as key resistance-associated druggable targets that are overexpressed in clear cell RCC (ccRCC) tumors and associated with patient poor overall survival. Functional validation confirmed that pharmacological inhibition of AXL and ENO2 effectively reduced cell viability of renal cancer cells. These findings unveil association of AXL and ENO2 with resistant phenotype in RCC cells, and reveal AXL and ENO2 as promising alternative therapeutic targets in renal cancer. SIGNIFICANCE: Acquired resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remains a major limitation in the treatment of renal cell carcinoma, underscoring the need to better understand the underlying mechanisms. In this study, we established lenvatinib- and cabozantinib-resistant renal cancer models to investigate shared resistance pathways. Quantitative proteomic analysis identified 35 proteins consistently upregulated in resistant cells, pointing to common adaptive mechanisms. Among these, AXL and enolase 2 were also overexpressed in patient tumors and associated with poor prognosis in ccRCC. Functional assays showed that inhibition of AXL and enolase 2 reduces the viability of renal cancer cells. Together, these findings identify proteins associated with the resistant phenotype that remain pharmacologically targetable and highlight potential targets for improving treatment of drug-refractory renal cancer.

articles.title: Purine and citrate metabolism in urolithiasis and bladder cancer: An integrated genetic, gene-expression, and targeted metabolite analysis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of bladder cancer (BC), but the contribution of inherited variation in purine and citrate metabolism remains incompletely understood. Because urolithiasis shares selected metabolic and epidemiological features with BC, we compared both disorders to identify shared and disease-specific molecular patterns. We analysed polymorphisms in ACLY, XDH, PNP, HPRT1, and GART together with targeted gene expression in peripheral blood-derived RNA and urinary citrate, hypoxanthine, and glycine measured by <sup>1</sup>H NMR in a Polish case-control cohort. Genetic associations were assessed using multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, smoking, and BMI, with BH-FDR correction. Genotype-expression, genotype-metabolite, and expression-metabolite relationships were evaluated, and peripheral findings were compared with GSE13507 and TCGA-BLCA bladder-tissue data. ACLY rs2304497 was associated with both diseases, whereas PNP rs1713420 showed a BC-specific association after multivariable adjustment and BH-FDR correction. XDH rs2295475 associations did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction, and formal interaction analyses provided no BH-FDR-significant evidence of effect modification. Peripheral ACLY and GART transcript abundance was lower in both disease groups, while PNP was additionally lower in urolithiasis. Urinary citrate and hypoxanthine were reduced only in urolithiasis. No cross-layer associations remained significant after adjustment and BH-FDR correction. In external bladder tissue, GART was increased in both datasets, while ACLY and HPRT1 were increased in paired TCGA-BLCA tumours. The findings indicate shared and disease-specific molecular patterns but do not support a simple linear relationship between inherited variation, peripheral transcript abundance, and urinary metabolites. Direct functional and tissue-specific validation is required.

articles.title: [Clinical analysis of 21 children with Xp11.2 translocation renal cell carcinoma].
articles.abstract: Objective: To summary the clinical characteristics, treatment and prognosis of children with Xp11.2 translocation renal cell carcinoma. Methods: In this case-series study, clinical data including sex, age, clinical manifestations, staging, treatment modalities, and follow-up outcomes of 21 children with Xp11.2 translocation renal cell carcinoma who first visit and received treatment and follow-up at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University from June 2019 to June 2025 were collected. The Kaplan-Meier method was used for survival analysis, and the Log-rank test was applied for univariate prognostic analysis. Results: Among the 21 children, 12 were males, 9 were females. The age at diagnosis was 15 (12, 16) years. Gross hematuria and flank pain were the main frequent symptoms, which occurred on 10 and 5 children respectively. According to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system, there were 7 children of stage Ⅰ, 2 children of stage Ⅱ, 9 children of stage Ⅲ, 3 children of stage Ⅳ. Children with stage Ⅰ-Ⅱ received surgical treatment only. With follow-up time of 19 (8, 52) months, none experienced disease recurrence. The 3-year event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) rates were both 100%. Among 9 children with stage Ⅲ, 4 received surgery alone, 2 of whom experienced recurrence; 5 received surgery plus tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), 1 of whom developed recurrence. Among 3 children of stage Ⅳ, 1 had extensive metastasis and was treated with sunitinib only, subsequently progressed and died; 1 received surgery plus sunitinib and later developed disease progression; 1 achieved partial remission after surgery combined with programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors and axitinib therapy. The progression or recurrence time was 7.0(6.5, 9.5) months. Among the 5 relapsed or progressive children, 1 child died; 4 children were treated with PD-1 inhibitor combined with axitinib, with 3 achieving complete remission and 1 obtaining stable disease. The follow-up duration for stage Ⅲ-Ⅳ children was 30.0 (12.8, 44.5) months, and the 3-year EFS and OS rates were 55% (95%CI 23%-78%) and 91% (95%CI 49%-97%), respectively. The follow-up duration for all 21 children was 28 (11, 44) months, with 3-year EFS and OS rates of 73% (95%CI 38%-91%) and 94% (95%CI 67%-99%), respectively. AJCC stage Ⅲ-Ⅳ and the presence of regional lymph node metastasis were both associated with disease progression and recurrence (both P<0.05). Conclusions: Children of Xp11.2 tRCC predominantly presents primarily with gross hematuria. Children with stage Ⅰ-Ⅱ can be treated with surgery alone, while those with stage Ⅲ-Ⅳ can receive surgical resection combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. The overall prognosis is favorable. AJCC stage Ⅲ-Ⅳ and the presence of regional lymph node metastasis are poor prognostic factors. PD-1 inhibitor combined with axitinib therapy can be used for the treatment of children with metastatic, recurrent or progressive disease.

articles.title: Temporal and therapeutic confounders in predicting efficacy of immunotherapy rechallenge via baseline intratumoral tertiary lymphoid structures.
articles.abstract: This correspondence discusses the recent multicenter study by Tang et al (2026) regarding the predictive value of baseline mature intratumoral tertiary lymphoid structures for immune checkpoint inhibitor rechallenge in non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma. While we commend the authors’ pioneering efforts, we raise critical methodological and biological considerations. First, the concurrent switching of tyrosine kinase inhibitors in nearly half the cohort acts as a major therapeutic confounding variable. Second, the biological plausibility of response conversion under class-refractory immunotherapy warrants cautious evaluation. Third, the extensive evolutionary stress during front-line therapy highlights a severe temporal decoupling between archival baseline tissue banking and post-resistance rechallenge outcomes. Finally, deeper mechanistic validation via spatial omics and comprehensive exhaustion panels is needed to strengthen these translational findings.

articles.title: Metabolic Reprogramming in Bladder Cancer: Molecular Drivers, Immune Regulation and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming is increasingly recognised as a central determinant of bladder cancer heterogeneity, immune regulation and treatment response. This review integrates genetic, epigenetic, microenvironmental and therapeutic evidence to explain how bladder cancer redistributes carbon and nitrogen across glycolysis, lipid synthesis and oxidation, amino-acid metabolism and mitochondrial respiration. Alterations in FGFR3, PIK3CA, MYC, TP53/RB1 and KDM6A establish distinct, context-dependent metabolic dependencies, while hypoxia, extracellular-matrix mechanics and treatment selection reinforce metabolic plasticity. These programmes influence not only energy production and biosynthesis but also ferroptosis, genome stability and chromatin or RNA regulation. Lactate, adenosine, kynurenine and asparagine further connect tumour metabolism to regulatory T cells, myeloid cells, innate immune sensing and CD8-positive T cell function, thereby shaping resistance to chemotherapy and immune-checkpoint blockade. Therapeutic opportunities include targeting glycolysis, fatty-acid and cholesterol metabolism, glutamine and proline metabolism, arginine auxotrophy and metabolite-mediated immune suppression. However, pathway redundancy, cellular heterogeneity and shared metabolic requirements between tumour and immune cells constrain unselected treatment. Urine, tissue, blood and imaging metabolomics offer complementary routes to diagnosis, prognostication and real-time response monitoring, but require harmonised sampling, functional flux measurements and prospective validation. A clinically useful strategy will therefore depend on defining metabolic vulnerabilities by genotype, cell type, spatial context and treatment stage, and on pairing pharmacodynamic biomarkers with rational combinations and local delivery where appropriate.

articles.title: Consumption of Processed Meat and Unprocessed Red Meat and Risk of Bladder Cancer: A Pooled Analysis of 30 Cohort Studies.
articles.abstract: Background: Processed meat and unprocessed red meat are considered carcinogenic and 'probably carcinogenic' to humans, respectively, but findings for bladder cancer remain inconsistent. Objectives: We assessed associations between processed meat and unprocessed red meat intake and bladder cancer risk using data from the Pooling Project of Prospective Studies of Diet and Cancer. Methods: Associations with bladder cancer risk were assessed using individual-level data from 30 cohort studies from North America, Europe, Australia and Asia. Diet was assessed at enrolment using validated food frequency questionnaires or diet histories. Following a pre-specified analysis plan, study- and sex-specific hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox regression, adjusted for smoking status and duration and other potential confounders, and pooled using inverse-variance-weighted random-effects meta-analysis. Results: During median follow-up across cohorts of 8-29 years, among 2,575,971 participants, 20,780 were diagnosed with bladder cancer. Processed meat intake was associated with increased bladder cancer risk (HR comparing ≥40 with <5 g/day = 1.08; 95% CI: 1.02-1.15; HR per 20 g/day = 1.02; 95% CI: 1.00-1.03). Weaker evidence of association with increased risk was also observed for unprocessed red meat (HR comparing ≥100 with <20 g/day = 1.06; 95% CI: 1.00-1.13; HR per 50 g/day = 1.01; 95% CI: 0.99-1.03). There was no evidence of heterogeneity by study, sex, or region. Conclusions: Higher intakes of processed meat and unprocessed red meat were associated with a small increase in risk of bladder cancer. These findings are consistent with existing public health recommendations to limit consumption of red and processed meat.

articles.title: Navigating the landscape of targeted therapies for renal cell carcinoma in the era of precision medicine (Review).
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a biologically heterogeneous malignancy characterized by dysregulation of angiogenic signaling, immune evasion and epigenetic remodeling. Advances in molecular profiling have redefined RCC as a pathway‑driven disease, enabling the development of targeted therapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) that have notably improved clinical outcomes. The present review evaluated current evidence on the molecular basis and therapeutic landscape of RCC, with emphasis on von Hippel‑Lindau‑hypoxia‑inducible factor signaling, chromatin remodeling alterations and immune regulatory pathways. The present review summarizes pivotal phase III clinical trials evaluating VEGF‑targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors, mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors and combination regimens, including nivolumab plus ipilimumab, pembrolizumab + axitinib and lenvatinib + pembrolizumab. Emerging biomarkers, including International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium risk stratification, programmed death‑ligand 1 expression and chromatin remodeling gene alterations (polybromo 1/BRG1‑associated factor 180, BRCA1‑associated protein 1 and SET domain containing 2), are discussed in the context of their clinical utility and limitations. Despite marked progress, durable predictive biomarkers and optimal treatment sequencing strategies remain unresolved. Resistance to therapy emerges through adaptive angiogenic signaling, immune escape and metabolic reprogramming, underscoring the need for integrated multi‑omics approaches and rational combination strategies. By integrating molecular biology with clinical trial evidence, the present review provides a structured framework for understanding therapeutic decision‑making in RCC and highlights future directions toward biomarker‑guided precision oncology.

articles.title: ROCK2 regulates a stress-responsive transcriptional state and calcium signaling in renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) exhibits marked intratumoral heterogeneity that contributes to disease progression and therapeutic resistance. Although ROCK2 has been implicated in RCC progression, its role in regulating tumor cell heterogeneity and cell-state plasticity remains poorly understood. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified a ROCK2-associated stress-responsive transcriptional state characterized by inflammatory signaling and enhanced calcium pathway activity. ROCK2 knockdown was associated with a lower representation of this transcriptional state together with proliferative tumor cells, and integration with the TCGA-KIRC cohort supported the presence of this stress-associated transcriptional program in bulk RCC tumors. Mechanistically, ROCK2 depletion reduced intracellular calcium levels, suppressed CALM1 and CREB1 expression, promoted apoptosis, and impaired cell-cycle progression and proliferation. Pharmacological restoration of calcium signaling with Bay K8644, together with CALM1 or CREB1 overexpression, partially rescued these defects, supporting functional interactions among ROCK2, calcium signaling, CALM1, and CREB1. Collectively, our findings identify a ROCK2-associated stress-responsive transcriptional state linked to altered calcium signaling and provide new mechanistic insight into RCC cellular heterogeneity, highlighting the functional relationship between ROCK2 and calcium signaling as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in RCC.

articles.title: Development and validation of a ferroptosis and metabolic reprogramming gene signature for risk stratification in bladder urothelial carcinoma: A retrospective multicohort study.
articles.abstract: Bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) is clinically and molecularly heterogeneous, and conventional clinicopathologic factors do not fully reflect the biological variation associated with survival. We aimed to develop and externally evaluate a prognostic signature based on genes related to both ferroptosis and metabolic reprogramming and to examine its clinical and biological associations. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-BLCA transcriptomic and clinical data were used for candidate-gene identification and model development. A 10-gene least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox signature was evaluated by complete-pipeline bootstrap validation. After platform harmonization, the same coefficients and TCGA-derived cutoff were applied to GSE13507 and GSE48075. Clinical adjustment, stage-specific analyses, immune analyses accounting for the IFNG score contribution, tumor purity, and molecular subtype, exploratory drug-response prediction, and expression analysis in 15 paired institutional tumor and adjacent tissues were performed. The signature comprised JUN, IFNG, CAV1, SREBF1, G6PD, TFRC, SCD, ZEB1, SLC7A11, and WWTR1. In TCGA-BLCA (401 patients; 176 deaths), the high-risk group had poorer overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.313; 95% confidence interval = 1.697-3.154; P < .001). The fixed TCGA cutoff also identified high-risk groups in GSE13507 (165 patients; 69 deaths; HR = 2.202; P = .0010) and GSE48075 (73 patients; 45 deaths; HR = 2.476; P = .0082). The 10-gene RiskScore yielded 1-, 3-, and 5-year areas under the curve of 0.644, 0.657, and 0.668 in TCGA-BLCA; the corresponding values ranged from 0.583 to 0.696 in the external cohorts. RiskScore remained associated with survival after adjustment for age, sex, and stage in TCGA (HR per standard-deviation increase, 1.573; P < .001). In the paired institutional cohort, 5 genes differed between tumor and adjacent tissues at a false discovery rate below 0.05, and 9 of 10 genes showed expression directions concordant with TCGA. Enrichment analyses highlighted oxidative-stress and metabolic pathways; several immune and checkpoint associations remained after sensitivity analyses, and exploratory modeling identified risk-group differences in predicted drug sensitivity. The 10-gene signature consistently stratified overall survival across TCGA-BLCA and 2 independent Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts. Its associations with clinical outcome, paired-tissue expression, and immune features support further investigation of ferroptosis-related metabolic heterogeneity in BLCA.

articles.title: Hyperdense Renal Lesion Characterization on Three DECT Technologies: Can Iodine Quantification Differentiate Hyperattenuating Renal Cysts From Papillary Renal Cell Cancers?
articles.abstract: To evaluate the performance of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) in differentiation of hyperattenuating renal cysts (HCs) from papillary renal cell cancers (pRCCs) on three different DECT technologies (dual-source [dsDECT], rapid kVp-switching [rsDECT], and dual-layer detector-based [dlDECT]). In this institutional review board-approved retrospective study, we included 85 patients with a total of 108 incidental hyperdense renal lesions detected on contrast-enhanced DECT scans (dsDECT, n = 41; rsDECT, n = 42; and dlDECT, n = 25). The study cohort included HCs (n = 73) and pRCCs (n = 35). Final confirmation was obtained with histopathology for pRCCs and with magnetic resonance imaging within 6 months of the DECT for HCs. Quantitative iodine evaluation was performed with iodine concentration (IC) measured within the lesion and the abdominal aorta. Normalized IC (NIC) was generated for each lesion by normalizing the lesion IC to the aortic IC. Both IC and NIC measurements yielded significant differences between HCs and pRCCs for the dsDECT and rsDECT techniques (P < 0.001) but not for the dlDECT (P > 0.05). Cutoff values with 100% sensitivity for pRCC detection were 0.30 and 0.60 mg/mL for dsDECT and rsDECT, respectively. Normalization to the abdominal aorta allowed creation of a uniform cutoff on both technologies, with an NIC value of 0.09 allowing 100% sensitivity for each. Significant intertechnique differences exist for the differentiation of HCs from pRCCs. Normalization of IC to the aorta provides a uniform cutoff for differentiation of these lesions on dsDECT and rsDECT.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Sequential Cabozantinib and Axitinib After First-Line Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab in Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Single-Center Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Evidence regarding sequential vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy after first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab in advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remains limited. This exploratory study described the clinical outcomes of sequential cabozantinib and axitinib administered as second- and third-line therapy, with additional analyses according to treatment order and early progressive disease (PD) status. We retrospectively reviewed 12 patients with advanced RCC who sequentially received cabozantinib and axitinib as second- and third-line therapy after first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab between September 2018 and January 2026. Patients were categorized into cabozantinib-to-axitinib (n=8) and axitinib-to-cabozantinib (n=4) groups. Tumor response was assessed according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1. Combined time to treatment failure (TTF) was measured from second-line initiation to progression during third-line therapy or death; event-free patients were censored at last follow-up. Among patients receiving second-line cabozantinib, three (37.5%) had stable disease and five (62.5%) had PD; among those receiving axitinib, three (75.0%) had a partial response and one (25.0%) had stable disease. Median second-line TTF was 5.1 months (interquartile range [IQR], 2.6-8.6) with cabozantinib and 10.1 months (IQR, 8.9-10.4) with axitinib (p=0.154). Median third-line TTF was 3.0 months (IQR, 1.6-13.6) with cabozantinib and 3.5 months (IQR, 2.7-5.7) with axitinib (p=0.808). Median combined TTF was 14.2 months for axitinib-to-cabozantinib and 10.4 months for cabozantinib-to-axitinib (p=0.359), and 8.3 versus 13.9 months in patients with early versus non-early PD (p=0.113). Sequential cabozantinib and axitinib therapy after nivolumab plus ipilimumab was feasible in selected patients with advanced RCC. Given the small exploratory cohort, no firm conclusion regarding the comparative efficacy of the two sequences can be drawn. Patients with early PD showed a numerical trend toward shorter combined TTF, although this comparison was statistically inconclusive.

articles.title: Efficacy of immune-oncology combinations versus sunitinib in patients with bone metastases from renal cell carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of phase III trials with long-term follow-up.
articles.abstract: Bone metastases occur in approximately one-third of patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and are associated with poor prognosis. Although immune-oncology (IO)-based combinations are the standard first-line treatment, the relative efficacy of IO plus tyrosine kinase inhibitor (IO+TKI) versus dual immunotherapy (IO+IO) in this subgroup remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of phase III randomized trials comparing first-line IO-based combinations with sunitinib in treatment-naïve metastatic ccRCC. Eligible studies reported hazard ratios (HRs) for progression-free survival (PFS) and/or overall survival (OS) in patients with baseline bone metastases and had a median follow-up of at least 36 months. The primary analysis pooled IO+TKI trials, whereas the single eligible IO+IO study was analyzed separately. Fixed- and random-effects inverse-variance models were applied. Three phase III trials were included: CLEAR (lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab versus sunitinib), CheckMate 9ER (nivolumab plus cabozantinib versus sunitinib), and CheckMate 214 (nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus sunitinib). IO+TKI significantly improved PFS versus sunitinib (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.35-0.61; p < 0.0001), with no heterogeneity (I2 = 0%). In contrast, IO+IO showed no PFS benefit (HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.76-1.51). Pooling all trials introduced substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 85.9%), and subgroup analysis confirmed a significant interaction between treatment class and PFS (p = 0.0002). IO+TKI also improved OS (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.88; p = 0.0041), again without heterogeneity (I2 = 0%). IO+IO showed a non-significant trend toward improved OS (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.61-1.11), with no significant difference between treatment classes for OS (p = 0.314). In patients with metastatic ccRCC and bone metastases, IO+TKI combinations were associated with significant improvements in PFS and OS compared with sunitinib, whereas IO+IO did not improve PFS. These findings suggest that treatment strategy may influence outcomes in this high-risk subgroup.

articles.title: Recurrent TFE3-Rearranged Renal Cell Carcinoma Responding to Pembrolizumab Plus Lenvatinib After Postoperative Pembrolizumab: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is rare, and evidence guiding systemic therapy is limited. A 25-year-old man with gross hematuria had a left renal tumor with hilar lymph node metastasis. Robot-assisted radical nephrectomy and hilar lymph node dissection were performed. Histology, immunohistochemistry, and fluorescence in situ hybridization confirmed TFE3-rearranged RCC, pT3aN1. Postoperative pembrolizumab was started because of the high risk of recurrence. Eight months after surgery, lung and retroperitoneal metastases developed. Lenvatinib was added to ongoing pembrolizumab. The metastatic lesions decreased within one month, and a partial response according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors has been maintained for ten months. This case suggests that adding a vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor to pembrolizumab may be a therapeutic option for recurrent TFE3-rearranged RCC, although longer follow-up and molecular characterization are needed.

articles.title: Chiral cerium doped nanoreactor-mediated bladder carcinoma reinforced ablation via fluorescence imaging navigated surgery along with photothermal strengthened ROS storm.
articles.abstract: Bladder cancer is regarded as one of the most prevalent malignant neoplasms of the urinary tract. However, the treatment of bladder cancer still presents unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes, especially for advanced patients. Chiral nanomaterials hold significant prospect for elevating clinical therapeutic effect, thanks to their unparalleled chiral selectivity in biological-systems. In this work, we have engineered chiral a cerium oxide (CeO2) doped mesoporous silica with, a photothermal and fluorescence contrast agent, indocyanine green loading (cSiCe&ICG). On account of the unique chiral nanostructure, this fascinating nanoreactor manifested effective enrichment in bladder tumor tissues and might be activated to mediate robust reactive oxygen species (ROS) under the weak acid and high H2O2 microenvironment of the tumor regions. Owing to the accurate tumor targeting and fluorescence intensification, increased tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) had been achieved for accurately discriminating tumor tissues from surrounding normal tissue. With the navigation of fluorescence imaging at second near-infrared region (NIR II, 1000-1700 nm), tumors could be completely removed. In particularly, with the aid of 808 nm light irradiation, the chiral Ce-based nanoreactor exhibited a high catalytic efficiency, by integrating photothermal that further mediating ROS production via Ce ions for bladder tumor cell eradication. These findings underscored the prospect of chiral nanoreactor for efficacious fluorescence bioimaging for guiding tumor surgery and synergistic tumor eradiation especially with the assistance of NIR light activation.

articles.title: METTL14-mediated FDX1 m6A methylation inhibited the proliferation of clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: FDX1 exerts a significant influence in the process of cuproptosis by facilitating the lipoacylation of proteins and reducing copper ions to monovalent copper ions. The methyltransferase METTL14 is an enzyme that modulates the m6A methylation of RNA, which can impact the stability, translation efficiency, and degradation rate of RNA. Nevertheless, the regulatory association between METTL14 and FDX1 in kidney cancer requires further investigation. The differential expression of METTL14 and FDX1 between normal tissues and renal cancer tissues was analyzed via the GEO public database. The association between these factors and patient survival was analyzed by utilizing the TCGA public database. A correlation analysis between METTL14 and FDX1 was performed based on the TCGA database. The findings were validated through RT - qPCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry assays. By using SRAMP tools and m6A correlation experiments, the study elucidated the reason for the decreased expression of FDX1 in renal cancer cells. In vivo and in vitro experiments were conducted to verify the regulatory effect of METTL14 on FDX1. In clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), METTL14 and FDX1 exhibit downregulation and are correlated with a poor prognosis among ccRCC patients. METTL14 augments the expression of FDX1 by enhancing the stability of the FDX1 messenger RNA. METTL14 upregulates FDX1 expression and consequently enhances cuproptosis in ccRCC cells. Methyltransferase METTL14 preserves the stability of FDX1 messenger RNA via m6A modification of FDX1 messenger RNA and acts as a crucial mediator of cuproptosis. Nevertheless, in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the level of cuproptosis declines as a result of the diminished expression of these two factors, and the proliferation capabilities of ccRCC cells are augmented.

articles.title: Nanoconfined Polymer Dot Reactors for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Diverse Metabolites and Point-of-Care Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Polymer dots (Pdots) offer high brightness and tunable electronic properties for point-of-care testing, but conventional sensing often suffers from inefficient stochastic interactions and limited adaptability. Here, we screened Pdots for interactions with the NAD+/NADH redox couple and identified PDFDP Pdots with an NADH detection limit of 2.41 nM. Coupling PDFDP Pdots with NAD+-dependent enzymes enabled detection of multiple metabolites through enzymatically generated NADH. Co-encapsulation of Pdots and enzymes within microreactors further enhanced signal transduction by spatial confinement. Combined with smartphone-based RGB analysis under UV illumination, the platform enabled micromolar detection of lactate, β-hydroxybutyrate, glutamate, alanine, and ethanol. The method was further demonstrated in sweat and urine samples, showing good agreement with established analytical methods and supporting its potential for portable metabolite monitoring and exploratory disease-associated analysis.

articles.title: Comparison of oral 5-aminolevulinic acid-induced hypotension between general and spinal anesthesia during photodynamic diagnosis-assisted transurethral resection of bladder tumor for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
articles.abstract: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) using photodynamic diagnosis (PDD) with oral 5-aminolevulinic acid hydrochloride (5-ALA) with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) frequently results in hypotension being reported as a common serious side effect. Previous papers have reported that oral 5-ALA-induced hypotension is associated with both general and spinal anesthesia However, no study has analyzed oral 5-ALA-induced hypotension by separately evaluating each anesthesia type. We retrospectively compared the systolic blood pressure (SBP) values with the frequency of vasopressor uses between general anesthesia group of 295 patients and spinal anesthesia group of 139 patients. Multivariable logistic regression analysis between general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups was performed for hypotensive patients with SBP less than 80 mmHg using vasopressors. A total of 434 patients who underwent PDD‑TURBT were included in the final analysis. The incidence of hypotension and the incidence of severe hypotension (among cases of hypotension) were determined for the general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups. The mean intraoperative lowest SBP was 73.1 mmHg in the general anesthesia group and 95.2 mmHg in the spinal anesthesia group (p < 0.001). In general anesthesia, older age, shorter 5‑ALA exposure, and lower initial SBP at the beginning of anesthesia predicted hypotension, whereas in spinal anesthesia, male sex and lower initial SBP at the beginning of anesthesia were significant predictors by multivariate analyses. The risk factors for oral 5‑ALA‑induced hypotension differ between the general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups, which is highlighting the importance of managing blood pressure while considering the specific risks associated with each type of anesthesia.

articles.title: Single‑cell multi‑omics analysis reveals TGF-β1-RUNX2-mediated matCAF differentiation and its role in remodeling the lymph node metastatic microenvironment in bladder cancer.
articles.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) in bladder cancer (BCa) is associated with poor clinical outcomes and may contribute to the development of metastatic tolerance, yet the stromal mechanisms underlying this process remain incompletely understood. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, clinical cohorts, and functional models, we identified an LNM-enriched matrix-remodeling cancer-associated fibroblast (matCAF) state characterized by LRRC15 and POSTN expression and associated with adverse survival and reduced immunotherapy response. Mechanistically, Hybrid_CCND1⁺ malignant epithelial cells promoted matCAF differentiation through FOS-dependent TGFB1 transcription and TGF-β1-TGFBR1-RUNX2 signaling. Spatial analyses further revealed barrier-like accumulation of matCAFs at tumor-stroma interfaces and linked matCAF-rich neighborhoods to enhanced PI3K activity and lymphangiogenesis-related programs. Functionally, matCAF-derived POSTN engaged ITGAV/ITGB5 to activate PI3K-AKT signaling and promote tumor and lymphatic endothelial remodeling. MatCAFs were also associated with SPP1⁺ macrophage remodeling and impaired CD8⁺ T-cell function, partly through RUNX2-associated CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling. Pharmacological disruption of the RUNX2-dependent matCAF program reduced tumor burden and partially restored T-cell activity in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify matCAF-centered stromal remodeling as a potential cellular basis of the metastatic-tolerance niche in BCa LNM and provide proof-of-concept for therapeutic targeting of the matCAF program.

articles.title: Balloon-occluded ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization of a hemorrhagic renal mass in an octogenarian initially unfit for nephrectomy.
articles.abstract: Palliative transarterial embolization is an established option for symptomatic renal tumors in patients who are poor surgical candidates, but conventional particle or coil techniques sacrifice uninvolved parenchyma and permit reflux-related non-target embolization. We report an 89-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who presented with one month of gross hematuria, transfusion-requiring anemia, and acute kidney injury secondary to a 5.8 × 4.6 × 3.4 cm hypervascular right upper-pole renal mass extending into the collecting system. Deemed unfit for nephrectomy during the index admission, he underwent super-selective balloon-occluded embolization with ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer delivered through a balloon-occlusion microcatheter. Hematuria resolved, hemoglobin stabilized without further transfusion, and creatinine returned to near baseline by post-procedure day 2. He remained free of hematuria for approximately 12 weeks despite resumption of apixaban. Recurrent intermittent bleeding from a persistent enhancing collecting-system component prompted readmission; surveillance imaging demonstrated a devascularized cortical tumor bed with an approximately 69% reduction in tumor volume and preserved parenchymal enhancement of the treated kidney. After interval stabilization, he underwent elective robotic nephrectomy with minimal blood loss. Pathology demonstrated clear cell renal cell carcinoma (grade 3, stage pT3a) with 50% tumor necrosis and post-embolization changes; urothelial carcinoma was excluded. Balloon-occluded ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization may provide effective temporizing hemostasis and histologically confirmed tumor devascularization in nonsurgical patients, serving in this case as a bridge to elective nephrectomy.

articles.title: Acquired Cystic Disease-Associated Renal Cell Carcinoma: Recurrent Copy-Number Patterns and Overlap With Papillary Renal Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Acquired cystic disease-associated renal cell carcinoma (ACD-RCC) is a histologically distinctive renal neoplasm arising in patients with end-stage renal disease, in which the molecular underpinnings remain incompletely characterized. In this study, 14 ACD-RCC tumors from 13 patients underwent comprehensive targeted next-generation sequencing with copy-number analysis. All tumors had classic histologic features characterized by solid sieve-like and cystic growth with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, predominantly high nucleolar grade (13/14), and variably present calcium oxalate crystals (10/14). By sequence analysis, single-gene alterations were relatively infrequent and heterogenous, with no recurrent alterations within the cohort; though several alterations identified were occasionally recurrent across studies on literature review (eg, KMT2C, SETD2, FANCA, and FAT1). Copy-number analysis identified 3 patterns of chromosomal alterations: gain-predominant (n=7), loss-predominant (n=4), and near-euploid (n=3) subgroups. Gain-predominant tumors harbored recurrent gains of chromosomes 3, 7, 16, 17, and 20, whereas loss-predominant tumors showed recurrent losses of chromosomes 6, 9, 14, 19, and 21. The near-euploid group had relatively fewer chromosomal copy-number alterations. Notably, comparison with publicly available The Cancer Genome Atlas papillary renal cell carcinoma (PRCC, TCGA-KIRP) data demonstrated overlapping gains of chromosomes 7, 16, 17, and 20 with the gain-predominant ACD-RCC. In addition, a paired ACD-RCC and synchronous PRCC from the same patient in our cohort displayed highly similar arm-level copy-number profiles, differing only by an additional gain of chromosome 3q in the ACD-RCC. In summary, ACD-RCC demonstrates recurrent arm-level chromosomal alteration patterns despite heterogenous gene-level findings. The gain-predominant tumors show substantial molecular overlap with PRCC, supporting genomic similarity between these entities despite distinct histomorphology. Together, these findings also suggest that copy-number patterns may represent a useful molecular framework for understanding heterogeneity within ACD-RCC.

articles.title: Drug-eluting bead transarterial chemoembolization with immunotherapy and targeted therapy for advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma: A case report.
articles.abstract: Abdominal wall metastasis is a rare metastatic pattern of clear cell renal cell carcinoma and is typically associated with advanced disease and poor prognosis. Due to its unique anatomical location and complex vascular supply, conventional systemic therapies have limited efficacy in controlling these metastases, and surgical resection is often challenging due to the deep-seated location of the tumor and its proximity to vital structures. Drug-eluting bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) is a promising locoregional therapeutic option for patients with refractory metastases. The present case report described a multimodal treatment strategy centered on DEB-TACE combined with an immune checkpoint inhibitor and a tyrosine kinase inhibitor in the treatment of this rare clinical scenario.

articles.title: A chitosan leaky waveguide biosensor for measurement of DNA biomarkers.
articles.abstract: Sustainable polymers such as chitosan are gaining popularity for diverse applications including sensing. Electrochemical sensors with chitosan-nanocomposite electrodes have been reported, but the use of undoped chitosan can reduce the cost of sensors. Chitosan films deposited on glass substrates can serve as optical label-free leaky waveguide (LW) sensors, providing high sensitivity at low cost compared to other optical sensors. Here, for the first time, we report chitosan LW biosensors for sequence-specific quantification of ∼7.9 kDa target DNA. The target DNA sequence selected in this work is strongly associated with low-grade, non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer. The chitosan LW biosensor offered a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.4 nM for the target DNA in buffer without amplification and an analysis time of 30 min. In comparison, the LOD for the target DNA in 50% and 100% synthetic urine was 18.7 and 33.2 nM, respectively.

articles.title: Multi-omics profiling of FFPE tissues identifies serine synthesis and impaired creatine metabolism as metabolic hallmarks of high-grade bladder cancer.
articles.abstract: High-grade (HG) bladder urothelial carcinoma is an aggressive tumor with poor outcomes, underscoring the need for early molecular stratification. However, a comprehensive functional understanding of its metabolic landscape remains limited. This study aims to delineate the proteomic and metabolic hallmarks of HG bladder cancer by leveraging formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue archives. We performed integrated proteomic (data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry) and untargeted metabolomic profiling on FFPE specimens from a discovery cohort of 56 patients (27 low-grade/LG, 29 HG). Key findings were validated via immunohistochemistry (IHC) on an independent cohort of 60 patients (30 LG, 30 HG). Proteomics revealed extensive molecular remodeling in HG tumors, with 2,506 differentially expressed proteins enriched in metabolic pathways. Metabolomics identified 67 altered metabolites, highlighting a profoundly rewired metabolic network. Integrated analysis converged on 2 core pathways: (1) enhanced nucleotide anabolism supported by the upregulation of enzymes including phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH), and (2) a collapsed creatine-phosphagen system evidenced by marked decreases in creatine/creatinine. IHC validation confirmed significant upregulation of PHGDH in HG tumors. Intriguingly, while metabolomic and DIA‑MS‑based proteomic data indicated downregulation of guanidinoacetate N‑methyltransferase (GAMT), the terminal enzyme for creatine biosynthesis, IHC on an independent validation cohort demonstrated robust GAMT immunoreactive accumulation within HG tumor cells. This multi‑omics discordance points toward complex, non‑canonical dysregulation consistent with a working model of protein‑catalytic‑function decoupling, which is presented as a testable working model requiring further experimental validation. This multi-omics study defines a metabolic dichotomy in HG bladder cancer, characterized by concurrent anabolic reinforcement and energy buffer collapse. We validate PHGDH as a consistent biomarker and uncover complex dysregulation of GAMT, consistent with a testable working model involving putative post-translational modifications, protein truncation, aberrant subcellular sequestration, or gain-of-non-canonical functions. Our findings provide novel metabolic biomarkers and reveal an unexpected layer of complexity in the molecular pathology of advanced bladder cancer.

articles.title: SLC25A28 is a synthetic lethal vulnerability in nucleotide excision repair-deficient cancers.
articles.abstract: Approximately 10% of bladder, upper urinary tract, and endometrial cancers harbor deleterious somatic alterations in nucleotide excision repair (NER) pathway genes. Although platinum-based chemotherapy is the standard treatment for NER-deficient tumors, its utility is limited by nephrotoxicity, motivating alternative strategies that avoid direct DNA targeting. Here, we employed a genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen to identify synthetic lethal vulnerabilities in NER-deficient cancer cells. An ERCC4 -null RT112/84 bladder cancer cell line was generated and validated by Sanger sequencing and Western blotting, and functional NER deficiency was confirmed using a host cell reactivation assay. Parallel screens in ERCC4 -deficient and isogenic wild-type cells. nominated SLC25A28 as the top-ranked synthetic lethal candidate in ERCC4 -deficient cells, an interaction further supported by DepMap dependency. Clonogenic assays confirmed that loss of SLC25A28 selectively impaired cell viability in cells deficient for ERCC2 , ERCC3 , ERCC4 , or ERCC5 and inducible knockout selectively suppressed ERCC4 -deficient xenograft growth in-viv o. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing followed by gene set enrichment analysis revealed enrichment of oxidative stress-related pathways, including cellular responses to reactive oxygen species (ROS) and DNA damage signatures, upon SLC25A28 loss. These transcriptional changes are consistent with increased oxidative stress and DNA damage, placing heightened demand on NER-mediated repair. Direct measurement confirmed increased intracellular ROS. Collectively, our nominates SLC25A28 as a previously unrecognized synthetic lethal vulnerability in NER-deficient cancers and implicate mitochondrial iron homeostasis as a candidate metabolic dependency that may be targeted independently of platinum-based chemotherapy. This study identifies SLC25A28 as a synthetic lethal vulnerability in nucleotide excision repair-deficient cancers, linking mitochondrial iron homeostasis and oxidative stress to selective DNA damage intolerance and therapeutic opportunity.
